summary.intent: Execute Session 5 of the v1-alpha launch plan: WP E (a NativeName type so registry-equivalent package names are one identity) and WP I (a directory index for relative `workspace:` npm dependencies). Then address a review finding on #561 about Cargo/npm historical tag ownership.
summary.outcome: Pushed PR #561 (E) and PR #563 (I), both with signed commits, green gates and trail #357 links. For the review finding, wrote a regression test, restored literal-name history ownership for non-PyPI ecosystems and committed it locally. The explicit-refspec push, ls-remote check and `entire trail finding` resolve were not yet done in the transcript.

repo: Package-name equivalence was enforced nowhere for Cargo; `package_id.rs` ~189 is `check_cargo_name`, which only checks characters. The plan's 'Cargo foo-bar/foo_bar is E100' decision had no code behind it, so WP E introduced it.
`ReleasePackageId.name` must stay a `String`: keying on NativeName would reorder serialized rosters and let a stored decision match a renamed package with differently spelled tags.

Default tags carry the literal package spelling (`{name}@`), so history/tag ownership must compare literal names for non-PyPI ecosystems. Registry equivalence is only correct for selectors, config rules and load-time duplicate detection.
Cross-ecosystem fallback and bare selectors intentionally match on exact spelling; only qualified selectors apply registry equivalence.
Callisto gates are `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test`. AGENTS.md also wants `just ci` before a PR is marked ready. Mutation testing runs via cargo-mutants on the diff.
Changesets are added with `callisto add --package <pkg>:patch --summary ...`. Summaries follow a bold-lead, Why-it-matters, **Action:** and **Limits:** format.
Commits must be signed (check `git log --format=%G?`). Trail linking uses `entire trail link <n> --base main` and `entire trail ci-pr`.
Equivalent-name workspaces that loaded before will now fail with E100, so the E changeset may need `**Breaking:**`. The owner has not decided.

code.finding: `may_have_held_name_at` returns early on a name match. With NativeName equivalence it wrongly attributed an npm `foo-bar` tag to a Cargo package renamed from `foo_bar`. The fix restored a local `names_equal` that uses PEP 503 for PyPI and literal comparison elsewhere.
TagIndex accepts a historical tag owner from the history check, so loosening history name comparison leaks foreign tags into the index.
Aggregation takes the version from the accepted historical tag as its baseline, so a wrongly attributed tag becomes a foreign baseline version.
`resolve_id` and `native_in_ecosystem` now do a single NativeName `get`. This fixes the E102 for `pypi/my-pkg` against `My_Pkg` and removes the PyPI ambiguity error arms.
`native_owner` is keyed on NativeName, which is the duplicate-detection fix that makes E100 fire for equivalent names.

workflow: Writing the regression test first and watching it fail before applying the fix worked as the lead asked.
BSD sed on macOS lacks GNU behaviors and needs `-i ''`, so multi-line edits went through python or perl scripts.
Python script edits bypass the worktree guard on the Edit tool. Editing a different worktree needs a proper EnterWorktree.
The first mutation run used a bad diff path filter and found only 3 mutants. Verify the mutant count against the diff scope before trusting a clean result.
Amending a pushed commit needed `--force-with-lease`. The lead's later instruction was explicit-refspec pushes and no rebase until #560 merges.
Delete `target/` in worktrees after use to free disk space.

friction: Fetching from GitHub required `github.com` to be allowed in the sandbox.
The first mutation-test run scoped the diff wrongly, giving a false sense of coverage. The re-run found 17 missed mutants.
Mechanical tuple-to-NativeName rewrites via regex needed several iterations to get the test code compiling.
Clippy flagged a duplicate `use super::*;` after test insertion, which forced an amend and force-push of #561.
A subagent design claimed some plan items were false or unneeded, such as the ReleasePackageId and release_decision changes. The plan and code needed cross-checking.
The final step merged `origin/worktree-wp-e-native-name` into the local branch after committing, which suggests divergence from the amend and force-push. The result was not shown.
open_items: Push the history fix on #561 with an explicit refspec, verify with `git ls-remote`, then resolve the review finding with `entire trail finding`.
Rebase #561 and then #563 only after the lead says #560 has merged. Resolve the `crates/callisto-cli/benches/commands.rs` conflict, keeping both A's change and the pnpm shape, then re-run the gates.
The owner must decide whether E's changeset counts as `**Breaking:**`. It stays unchanged for now.
Glob patterns like `pypi/my-*` still match the manifest spelling rather than the canonical name. This needs a code comment or a follow-up.
The one missed mutant (empty `Hash::hash` for NativeName) is equivalent and needs a line in the PR body.
#561's audit failure (RUSTSEC-2026-0542) is fixed by #560's `deny.toml` change, so no ignore was added.
`just ci` was not run on either PR.
Both worktrees remain on disk and should be deleted after merge.
The owner should confirm that Cargo `foo-bar`/`foo_bar` should be E100.
Confirm the local branch state after the final `git merge origin/worktree-wp-e-native-name`, then re-run the E gates on the final commit.
